PullRequest.Title: sessions: stabilize and toggle the default PR activity action
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #343635 and #343557.

## Changes

- Keep the PR activity action stable during metadata refreshes: opener checks depend on reference identity and URI, not titles, and confirmed support remains visible during capability revalidation.
- Make the checked PR action collapse the side pane; activating it again reveals the existing editor. Preserve existing-editor reuse and first-supported-PR fallback.
- Show supported PR actions automatically, without a separate setting, enable command, or context-menu switch.
- Remove the Issue activity action for now, preserving Issue composer pills and navigation.
- Update accessibility help, fixtures, and regression coverage.

## Validation

- `npm run compile` — passed.
- `npm run hygiene` — passed, 13,968 files checked.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob '**/{sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser,sessions/contrib/github/test/browser,sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser,sessions/test/browser}/**/*.test.js'` — passed: 4,370 tests, 3 pending.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed after rebasing onto main.
- Independent reviews of both implementation deltas — no significant issues found.
- Before rebasing: 148 affected component fixtures rendered without errors; light and high-contrast PR states inspected. Nine-step Code OSS scenario passed, covering automatic visibility, no opt-in menu, stable metadata refreshes, pending opener revalidation, PR toggling, Issue composer preservation, and actual reference removal.

The live scenario used synthetic references and overview editors in the real dev workbench. Live GHPR-extension integration remains explicitly out of scope, as agreed. No screenshot hashes were generated locally.

## How to Test

1. Enable the Session Activity Bar and open a chat with PR references and an available contributed URI opener.
2. Confirm the PR action appears automatically in the side-pane group, without a PR-specific enable setting or switch.
3. Refresh PR metadata and confirm the action does not disappear and reappear.
4. Activate the PR action to open or reveal its editor. Activate the checked action to collapse the side pane, then activate it again to restore it.
5. Confirm Issue actions are absent from the activity bar while Issue composer pills still work.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed default gate, lazy-observable subscription, extension activation, and per-opener RPC call path are all explicit in repository code. The exact wall-time varies with installed opener extensions and session size, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Extension activation work and extension-host `$canOpenUri` IPC calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each loaded chat group, the toolbar probes every deduplicated pull-request URI concurrently; after HTTPS activation is coalesced once, warm checks still issue one `canOpen` RPC per URI per registered opener, with no cache shared across chat groups.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Background extension activation and IPC/CPU bursts during session restoration or chat switching, increasing contention and latency as split chats and referenced pull requests grow.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The removed `sessions.sessionActivityBar.showGitHubActions` gate defaulted to false, so ordinary session views did not evaluate `activityBarOpeners` and performed no opener activation or support IPC until users explicitly opted in.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new condition evaluates opener support whenever pills are visible. Every enabled `SessionActivityBar` observes each group's `activityBarActions` even when that bar is marked inactive, so loading a chat with PR references now starts these checks automatically.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 617 removes the former `!gitHubActionsEnabled.read(reader)` short-circuit. Since the removed setting defaulted to false, this line newly allows the existing per-reference `getOpener` loop to execute automatically for normal chats.
Findings.Title: Defer opener probing to the active chat
Findings.Impact: Opening or restoring an Agents window with PR-bearing split chats can activate HTTPS opener extensions (including the built-in Simple Browser) and fan out extension-host support checks for hidden/inactive activity bars. Rendering is not awaited, but this newly eager work competes with restoration and retains the activated extension for the window lifetime.
Findings.Evidence: `activityBarActions` reads `activityBarOpeners`, which maps each ref through `externalUriOpenerService.getOpener`. That service calls each provider's `getOpeners`; `MainThreadUriOpeners.getOpeners` awaits `activateByEvent('onOpenExternalUri:https')`, and validation invokes `proxy.$canOpenUri` for every registered opener. `ChatGroupView` installs the observable on each group's `SessionActivityBar`, whose autorun reads it whenever the activity-bar setting is enabled; `setActive` only changes CSS and does not stop observation. `getSessionGitHubReferences` deduplicates within one chat, but there is no cross-group result cache.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep automatic visibility, but start support probing only for the currently active, enabled activity bar and coalesce/cache checks by URI across chat toolbars; invalidate the shared results on extension or external-opener configuration changes.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Full GitHub reference objects were dependencies of the support derivation, so metadata-only changes reran per-reference external-opener discovery and extension-host canOpen IPC.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Refreshing unchanged PR metadata repeatedly caused repeated opener support lookups, as demonstrated by the new test that applies ten title updates and expects no new lookups.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added ID-and-URI-only observable remains equal across title refreshes, preventing those opener checks while still invalidating for a changed reference or URL.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 620 reads complete PR and issue refs into the opener check. RIGHT line 612 adds a structurally compared projection containing only ID and URI, and line 621 uses it. ExternalUriOpenerService reaches opener activation and canOpen IPC, so each avoided invalidation removes concrete boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore an Agents chat with pull-request references while the Session Activity Bar is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat rendering does not await opener discovery because the code launches `Promise.all` without awaiting it; however, PR action availability waits for the checks, and extension activation plus IPC runs concurrently with restoration and can contend for CPU/extension-host resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate extensions for `onOpenExternalUri:https`, then call each registered external opener's `canOpenExternalUri` through `$canOpenUri`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For G loaded chat groups, U deduplicated PR URLs per group, and O registered openers, cold activation is coalesced per activation event/extension host, but validation performs up to G*U*O opener RPCs. There is no cross-group URI cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed opt-in setting defaulted false, so normal chats short-circuited before support discovery and issued zero activation/support calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the direct render critical path, but required before the PR activity action appears and concurrent with session restoration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective input is unique PR links after per-chat `dedupeByLink`, multiplied by loaded chat groups and registered external openers; split/inactive groups remain subscribed even though only the active activity bar is shown.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All PR URLs in one toolbar are checked with unbounded `Promise.all`; independent chat groups do the same. Extension-event activation is internally coalesced, but per-URI/per-opener validation IPC is not globally limited or coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold checks activate matching HTTPS opener extensions, including Simple Browser. Warm checks skip repeated activation through the extension manager's event cache but still execute `canOpen` RPCs. Support is retained only inside one toolbar and there is no cross-toolbar cache; extension/config changes invalidate and recheck.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default-gate removal, observable subscription for inactive groups, activation event, and extension-host RPC path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most chats likely have one PR and few openers, while split sessions or artifact-heavy chats increase the burst. Exact extension activation and RPC cost depends on installed extensions and remote extension-host placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: the PR intentionally makes actions automatic, but it eagerly probes hidden/inactive groups and fans out support IPC that can be deferred and coalesced without changing visible behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh PR title/status metadata without changing reference identity or URI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Metadata refresh updates observables used by the toolbar. After this PR, the opener-support boundary is no longer entered for title-only updates, so no additional work blocks or competes with refresh handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: External opener discovery and `canOpenExternalUri` validation that previously repeated after metadata-only invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the fix, each metadata refresh could repeat U*O checks; after the URL/ID projection, zero additional checks occur until a URI/ID or opener registry/configuration changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Complete reference objects, including changing metadata, invalidated the support derivation and reran opener checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The PR removes repeated asynchronous boundary work from metadata refreshes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of metadata refreshes times unique PR URLs and registered openers before the fix; reduced to zero for metadata-only changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Previously each invalidation launched all URL checks concurrently; now such refreshes reuse the existing result.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The structurally compared ID/URI projection acts as an invalidation filter. Changed URLs and extension/opener configuration events still revalidate, while title changes preserve support.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; changed dependency shape and test-observed lookup count directly establish the removed work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh frequency varies by provider, but the mechanism is directly covered by a ten-refresh regression test.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a concrete repeated-work performance fix and was recorded with its introducing commit; it is not a review finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the PR activity action to hide, reveal, reuse, or open a PR editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The checked action now synchronously hides the side pane and returns. Otherwise it scans already-open editors in-process, then either reveals an existing editor or dispatches the existing first-entry open action. The editor reveal/open remains user-triggered and on the action critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: When no matching editor exists, the existing pill entry may dispatch through the contributed opener to open the PR overview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open dispatch per user activation; existing-editor reuse and checked-action collapse issue no boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The opted-in action already reused an editor or opened the first supported reference. The PR changes checked activation to hide the pane, which is an in-process layout operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The contributed open must complete for a newly opened PR editor, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Editor matching scans the current editor list and PR entries; typical cardinality is small and the scan existed before the change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One user action is handled serially; no new burst or limiter change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previously discovered support is reused until URI/extension/config invalidation. Existing editors avoid a new open dispatch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call flow; no new expensive mechanism beyond the separately reported eager support probing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor-list size varies, but the diff does not increase scan frequency or complexity enough to establish a separate regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display issue references and composer pills after removing the Issue activity action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Issue composer rendering remains in-process. The activity-bar support probe now excludes issue refs, so issue-only chats perform no external-opener support lookup for the activity bar.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of issue references affects existing composer/model work, but the diff removes issue activity checks rather than adding them.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No issue opener-probe concurrency remains on this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No activity-bar issue support cache is populated; composer/model caching behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the diff's performance effect.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files. Submitted one medium eager-work/IPC finding for automatic opener probing across inactive chat groups, and recorded the PR's separate metadata-refresh repeated-work fix using blame.
